items.title: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
items.topic: Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency
items.summary: The arXiv paper 'Cognitive Dual-Process Planning for Autonomous Driving with Structured Scene Knowledge and Verifiable Reasoning-Action Consistency' presents a cognitive dual-process planning framework for autonomous driving, which represents planning-relevant scene knowledge in a machine-parsable structured chain-of-thought schema. This framework integrates perception foundation models, critical-path filtering, and an expert VLM to generate supervision without costly structured annotation. The approach aims to improve the consistency between generated rationales and driving actions. Researchers from arXiv published this paper on July 21, 2026, highlighting the importance of explainability in autonomous driving. This study has a score of 98 for its relevance to AV research.

items.title: A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving
items.topic: A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving
items.source: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
items.summary: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems published 'A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving' on May 27, 2026, introducing a large language model-based game equilibrium selection approach for human-machine shared driving authority allocation. This approach seamlessly transitions between Stackelberg equilibrium and Nash equilibrium, addressing human-dominated and human-machine equal relationships. The selection process is based on a game equilibrium selection model, which is developed to address the gap between theory and reality in human-machine shared driving. This study has significant implications for AV trust and acceptance, with a score of 95 for its relevance to AV research.

items.summary: The arXiv paper 'D3VL: Understanding Driving Scenes from 3D Time Series Data and Video with Language Models' proposes a novel MLLM framework that integrates 2D and 3D data for autonomous driving, using a pre-trained video VAE to encode video latents and a global semantic codebook to unify observations into a shared vocabulary. Published on July 21, 2026, this study demonstrates the effectiveness of MLLMs in using 3D sensors, particularly LiDAR and stereo cameras, for end-to-end autonomous driving. The D3VL framework improves performance in traditional 3D scene perception tasks, with a score of 96 for its relevance to AV research, highlighting the importance of multimodal perception in autonomous vehicles.
